dedupe_keys.name: open access model for detecting openly dumped municipal solid waste in crowdsourced uav imagery sub saharan africa and yolo swag

description: This open model detects openly dumped, dispersed municipal solid waste in drone imagery of towns and cities in Sub-Saharan Africa. A fine-tuned YOLO11x classifier labels each 5 m by 5 m tile of an OpenAerialMap scene as waste or background, and the share of waste tiles gives a contamination measure for each area, which the study relates to street-network complexity and population density from the Million Neighborhoods Africa data. The provider is the GIScience group and HeiGIT at Heidelberg University, with Steffen Knoblauch as creator of the archived release; a follow-on model, YOLO SWAG, extends the labels by country and city for the fAIr mapping tool. Coverage is 29 study regions in 10 countries; the preprint (arXiv 2605.02316) finds hotspots along waterways, where waste can worsen flooding and health risks. The Python pipeline, trained weights and labels are on GitHub and archived on Zenodo as v3.0.0; the README states the MIT licence while the Zenodo deposit lists CC-BY-4.0, so users should check which applies to which part. Caveats: detection needs recent high-resolution drone imagery, crowdsourced scenes are patchy in time and space, and small or covered waste is missed. Simulation uses: mapping dumped waste that blocks drains before flood season, targeting collection services, and exposure of informal settlements to waste-related hazards. Related records: What a Waste (data-world-waste-status) gives national waste statistics.
